- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought traps.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model often fails to mean-revert; force 14-day MA alignment for next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of lag.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or negative, model tends to ignore downward momentum; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid “false optimism” bias.
